doc.title: Carmen Lundy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 15, 2023

title: Taking original songs to Brewster, and his limits with jazz charts
summary: She cannot recall bringing songs; later in New York she studied again with Brewster and found he did not know jazz chord jargon.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: That’s terrific because the jazz education was not established like it is now, so the fact that you had that positive experience is very nice to hear. I wonder if you ever brought an original song to your lessons at that time?

Oh gosh, oh my God you’re asking me — that’s okay. I don’t remember but I do recall at some point — oh no that was in my New York days because Dr. Brewster moved to New York three years after I moved to New York and I picked up my studies again with him.

And that’s when I realized that for an amazing of a pianist, he didn’t understand the jazz theory and the jazz jargon so if I handed him a chart and the chart said A minor seven/ D seven/G, he didn’t know what to do because it wasn’t written out. You know what I mean? So but other than that I just never really — I’m trying to think did I — I don’t remember. I’m sorry, I wish I could.
